forces.title: Escalating Cyber Risks and Major Attacks in the UK
forces.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector continues to face significant and rising cyber risks, notably following major attacks in 2025. This creates near-term uncertainty and demands robust cybersecurity measures. The persistent threat environment necessitates continuous investment and adaptation by cybersecurity firms to protect critical digital infrastructure and services, particularly in the UK. The severity of past attacks underscores the ongoing vulnerability and the critical role of the cybersecurity industry.

forces.title: AI Adoption Drives Accelerated Cybersecurity Spending Growth
forces.description: AI adoption is widely expected by CISOs to drive a sustained acceleration in cybersecurity spend growth, with nearly half forecasting increased budgets. This indicates that despite potential productivity gains, AI's expansion of the digital attack surface and creation of new threats necessitate greater investment in security. For cybersecurity companies, this translates into a strong market tailwind, as organizations prioritize enhanced defenses to secure AI systems and mitigate AI-enabled attacks.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

forces.title: New Cyber and Data Privacy Risks from AI Applications
forces.description: AI applications and technologies are significantly expanding the digital attack surface, introducing new cyber and data privacy risks. Organizations report experiencing numerous AI-enabled attacks, including targeted social engineering, malware, fraud schemes, and vulnerability exploitation, often with significant operational or financial impact. This necessitates cybersecurity firms to innovate rapidly, develop solutions specifically for AI systems, and enhance threat intelligence capabilities to counter these evolving, AI-powered threats.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

forces.title: Increasing Demand for AI-Powered Security Capabilities
forces.description: As AI fuels new threats, it also offers powerful defense mechanisms. Practitioners are becoming more comfortable with Generative AI-powered security tools, and a significant portion plan to adopt AI-powered Security Operations Center (SOC) triage. This creates a substantial opportunity for cybersecurity providers to integrate advanced AI capabilities into their products and services, enhancing detection, response, and automation to combat sophisticated threats more effectively and efficiently.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

forces.title: Low Adoption of AI-Specific Security Controls
forces.description: Most organizations have adopted minimal AI-specific security controls, indicating a significant gap in protecting against AI-related threats such as data leakage to GenAI tools, shadow AI, and AI vulnerability exploitation. This lack of robust defense mechanisms leaves organizations exposed. For cybersecurity firms, this represents a critical, unmet need and an opportunity to provide specialized AI security solutions, but also highlights a challenge in educating the market and driving adoption of these new controls.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

forces.title: Regulation and Compliance Driving Demand in Critical Infrastructure
forces.description: Updated cyber strategies and legislation in the UK are introducing increasingly high expectations for suppliers, particularly within Critical National Infrastructure (CNI). Cybersecurity is recognized as underpinning the integrity of essential services and the economy. This regulatory push, combined with growing interdependencies across digital and physical systems, creates a strong demand signal for cybersecurity firms to provide solutions that embed resilience, ensure compliance, and support national preparedness efforts.

forces.title: Agentic AI Increases Need for Verified Identities and Liability
forces.description: The rise of agentic AI, particularly in consumer and corporate financial activities, introduces new challenges around 'delegated authorization, verified agent identities, and clear supervisory liability frameworks.' As autonomous agents perform tasks on behalf of users, the need for robust identity and access management (IAM) solutions, as well as frameworks for accountability, becomes paramount. This represents a fundamental shift creating new requirements for the cybersecurity sector to secure these new digital identities and their actions.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI Drives Demand for API and Data Orchestration Security
forces.description: Agentic AI necessitates secure, modular architectures with clearly defined APIs and permission-aware intelligence layers. As agents interact across disparate systems and workflows, the need for API/runtime protection, monitoring and logging of agent actions, and governance for non-human identities becomes critical. Cybersecurity firms providing API security, data orchestration security, and zero-trust IAM solutions will find increased demand as enterprises adopt agentic workflows and expose more capabilities via APIs.
forces.source_title: Agentic AI and the New Complexity Trap in Enterprise Software

forces.title: Evolving Governance for Decentralized AI Decision Making
forces.description: As AI shifts decision-making down the organizational chart and employees gain autonomy with AI agents, software companies face 'organizational chaos unless their governance is built for an agentic world.' This demands evolved management systems and clear decision rights regarding human-in-the-loop and autonomous agent actions, including accountability when errors occur. Cybersecurity, particularly in identity and access management and policy enforcement for AI agents, will be critical in enabling this decentralized, agentic operating model.
forces.source_title: How Will AI Change Software Organizations?

viewpoints.title: Rising Cyber Risks a Key Concern Amid Major Attacks
viewpoints.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector faces near-term uncertainty due to rising cyber risks, specifically highlighted as a key concern following major attacks in 2025. This indicates a sustained threat landscape requiring enhanced cybersecurity measures. Chris Daker, Sector Head, emphasizes that businesses need to carefully manage cyber risks alongside other challenges like energy and supply-chain pressures, despite overall sector resilience. The implication for cybersecurity firms is a continued demand for their services driven by persistent threats.

viewpoints.title: AI Adoption to Accelerate Cybersecurity Spend Growth
viewpoints.description: Cybersecurity Information Security Officers (CISOs) anticipate that the widespread adoption of AI will lead to a sustained acceleration in cybersecurity spending growth. Nearly half (49%) of respondents believe AI adoption will increase cyber spend, rather than offsetting it through automation or productivity gains. This indicates a strong belief within the industry that AI, while offering productivity benefits, primarily expands the threat landscape and necessitates increased investment in security measures, driving demand for cybersecurity solutions.
viewpoints.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

viewpoints.title: AI Amplifies Both Cyber Risks and Defense Capabilities
viewpoints.description: AI applications and technologies are creating new cyber and data privacy risks, significantly expanding the digital attack surface. At the same time, AI is also powering defenses. Organizations report experiencing numerous AI-enabled attacks (89%), often with significant impact (35%), while simultaneously planning to adopt AI-powered security tools (33% for SOC triage in 2026). This dual role of AI suggests a transformative period for cybersecurity, where innovation is crucial for both offense and defense.
viewpoints.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.

viewpoints.title: Cyber Security Underpins UK Critical Systems Resilience
viewpoints.description: Cybersecurity is foundational to the integrity of government functions, essential services, information flow, and the economy, especially for Critical National Infrastructure (CNI). As the UK government advances cyber and resilience strategies, public-private partnerships are crucial to address threats and improve long-term capability. Updated cyber strategies and legislation are introducing increasingly high expectations for suppliers. This signifies a strong and growing imperative for robust cybersecurity solutions across the UK's critical sectors, driving demand and innovation for providers.

viewpoints.title: AI Infusion Presents Both Opportunity and Risk for SaaS
viewpoints.description: The gradual infusion of AI into corporate processes is revamping IT requirements and presents both a business opportunity (due to a low learning curve for adoption) and a risk (potential dilution of SaaS revenue and margin). For cybersecurity companies operating on a SaaS/managed services model, this means new opportunities to integrate AI-driven security features and address AI-related risks, but also the challenge of adapting pricing and business models to avoid margin erosion in a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

demand_drivers.description: AI applications are creating new cyber and data privacy risks, expanding the digital attack surface, and enabling faster, more scalable, and frequent attacks, directly driving the need for increased cybersecurity investment.

Continued cloud migration and the increasing volume of data drive demand for cloud workload and container protection, data security posture management, and data loss prevention/insider threat solutions.
Growing complexity and evolving threats lead to increased adoption of managed detection and response (MDR) services, as organizations seek external expertise and continuous monitoring.

new_opportunities.description: High demand for new solutions specific to securing AI applications, including protection against data leakage to GenAI tools, shadow AI monitoring, and AI vulnerability exploitation. 69% of respondents reported increasing spend in this area.

Significant increases in spending for Extended Detection and Response (XDR), Network Detection and Response (NDR), and Endpoint Protection, indicating a need for integrated and comprehensive threat detection capabilities.

Strong growth in areas like Cloud Workload and Container Protection, and Cloud Access Security/Secure Web Gateway, driven by continued cloud adoption and the need to secure distributed cloud environments.

market_sizing.methodology: Survey data from N=302 CISOs across various companies in March 2026, asking about changes in cybersecurity spend year-over-year.
market_sizing.source_title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.
